_doc: Conkers (core/conkers.gd). A conker is a horse chestnut on a string; players take turns to swing at each other's. hits is how many whole blows it takes before it breaks; a seasoned conker takes more. skill is how often a rival's swing lands true. prize is whole pounds, paid once a real day per rival.

rivals.who: Mrs Pettifer from the post office

plaque.title: The World Conker Championships
plaque.text: Conkers is played with the seeds of the horse chestnut, Aesculus hippocastanum, a tree that came to Britain from the Balkans in the 1600s. Each player threads a conker on a string and the two take turns to swing at one another's until one breaks. The World Conker Championships have been held at Ashton in Northamptonshire since 1965, on the second Sunday of October, and raise money for charity. The organisers supply the conkers and the string, so nobody can bake theirs or soak them in vinegar. Both are well known cheats.
